name: listing-credits-an-individual-producer
rule: A rental room's listing can credit an INDIVIDUAL as producing the show rather than a company (#2554), and since that change `organisationNamedOnListing` may hold a person's name despite the field's name. That person owns the show and could hire Dan, so they are a research target pursued exactly as a company is: through their own site, starting with the canonical firstnamelastname.com guess, and emitted with `provenance: "presenter"` alongside the performers the listing names. The room stays refused.

expected.description: Modelled on the real 2026-08-13 run that raised #2554 to p0. On '54 Sings Shuffle Along' the run was handed listing text saying the concert was produced and directed by a named individual, READ that text (all 13 cast names came out of it), and returned 13 contacts, every one a co-performer and not one with authority over the booking. The producer was never a target, and her address was published on the first domain anybody would guess. So `requiredEmails` pins the producer's own address rather than merely counting contacts: a run that comes back with two form-only performers looks complete on every count-based check and is precisely the outcome being regressed against. The performers are still pursued, because the producer is additive and never a replacement. The room's inboxes stay refused: naming a producer relaxes nothing about the venue rule. NOTE the harness has no expectation key for a contact's `tier`, so this fixture proves the producer is REACHED and does not assert she comes back as `primary`; #2641 is the issue positioned to notice a run that ignores the tier instruction.

contacts.name: Theo Branch
contacts.overrideBody: My name is Dan and I'm a professional arts photographer here in New York City. I'm writing in regard to Ten Years of Tuesdays at The Example Room on August 17. I shoot unobtrusive, no-flash documentary coverage, so the audience doesn't notice me and the performance isn't disturbed. I've been photographing at Carnegie Hall for close to ten years, and you can see my portfolio at danwrightphotography.com. If you don't have someone on it already, I'd be glad to talk about your photography plans for the night. I look forward to hearing from you.
